methodology.method_family: environmental soil science field sampling and laboratory analysis
methodology.study_design: cross-sectional field sampling with physicochemical characterization, trace element analysis (ICP-MS), and toxicological bioassays (Caenorhabditis elegans)
methodology.sample_description: Soil and sediment samples collected at nine sampling points in a tropical dry forest area in the Caribbean region of Colombia, at 20 cm depth, approximately 1 kg each
methodology.technology_context: ICP-MS trace element analysis, standardized physicochemical soil methods, C. elegans ecotoxicological bioassays; no AI or LLM systems

synthesis.main_claim: Open-air dumping of urban solid waste causes slight to moderate soil deterioration and contamination by Ni, Cu, and Cd in a tropical dry forest environment in Colombia, with implications for environmental policy and monitoring.
synthesis.contribution: Provides baseline physicochemical and toxicological data on soil and sediment impacts of open dumping to inform environmental policies and sustainable waste management with local stakeholders.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from central and supporting evidence. Not usable as foundational context for LLM conversational governance because the governance, risk, monitoring, and responsibility references are environmental, not AI-related. May be noted only as a keyword false-positive example in screening QA.
